title: Mindagold Carrot (Mindagold F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Mindagold carrot is an F1 hybrid carrot variety from Ramgo. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Mindagold carrot is an F1 hybrid carrot variety, also sold or known as Mindagold F1. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Ramgo.

heroImage.alt: Vegetable terraces and plastic tunnels on the slopes of Mankayan, Benguet, the kind of farm where Mindagold carrot is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Mindagold F1, this is the same carrot. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [carrot variety finder](/crop-varieties/carrot), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).

blocks.caption: From its seller and farm sources
rows: Days to harvest, per the seller

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: harvest 90 to 100 days after sowing. Yield, by the seller's count: 30 to 40 t/ha potential (company figure). No trial on record checks these figures yet, so treat them as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit carrot fields most often: [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [leafminer](/pests/leafminer), [root knot nematode](/diseases/root-knot-nematode). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** Harvest 90 to 100 days after sowing.
**Fruit:** Root: 13 to 20 cm long and 4 to 5 cm across, bright orange inside and out.
Tolerates alternaria leaf blight and bolting.

blocks.text: These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual carrot on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Mindagold carrot

Carrot is a highland crop in the Philippines. Pick a root length your soil can hold: short types for heavy soil. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Mindagold F1 the same as Mindagold?
items.a: Yes. Mindagold F1 is another name for Mindagold. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Mindagold?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
